thesisQuality.note: Strong demand/adoption evidence in cooling components, but consolidated AI economics are undisclosed, keeping the assessment inside the strong band rather than exceptional.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Revenue and operating earnings grew year over year and segment bookings/book-to-bill show demand visibility; acquisition/mix effects limit a higher anchor.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Current market capitalization is about $25.2B while retrieved evidence does not establish a compelling forward-multiple discount; therefore valuation is treated as mixed/balanced, not favorable by default.

catalystScore.note: Capacity expansion for AI data-center heat transfer plus strong bookings are identifiable current catalysts, but exact earnings contribution/timing is not separately quantified.

governancePower.note: Current primary reporting supports functioning execution and disclosure, but this run lacks source-addressed evidence sufficient for a strong stewardship/capital-allocation anchor; uncertainty is retained in the mixed band.

alignment2036.note: Liquid-cooling connectors and heat exchangers directly serve rising thermal-management needs from dense compute while Dover also operates diversified industrial capabilities.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Dover has diversified industrial demand engines and multiple cooling-component exposures; however AI economics are not independently disclosed as a separate engine.

bottleneckControl.note: Capacity investment and specialized cooling components show meaningful constraint participation, but evidence does not establish system-critical scarcity or prohibitive switching costs.

scenarioRobustness.note: Diversified industrial exposure provides multiple demand paths beyond AI cooling, while acquisition/macro/customer-capex sensitivity prevents a higher robustness anchor.

substitutionResilience.note: Specialized connector/heat-transfer capability creates moderate replacement barriers, but OEM insourcing and alternative cooling architectures remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.note: Primary reporting identifies supply-chain/input risks and capacity expansion, but does not demonstrate tested multi-source redundancy sufficient for a strong anchor.

pricingPower.note: Operating earnings growth alongside revenue growth supports some value capture, but direct pass-through/scarcity-rent evidence for cooling products is not disclosed.

risk.note: Material but non-gating risks include acquisition/mix opacity, competition/pricing, supply-chain/input exposure, customer capex sensitivity and cooling-architecture/OEM substitution.

confidence.note: Identity/tradability and five unique primary origins are validated with no unresolved contradiction; confidence is reduced for thin independent corroboration and undisclosed AI-specific economics/customer concentration.

thesis: Dover combines diversified industrial cash-generation with specialized liquid-cooling and heat-transfer components positioned for higher-density compute demand; the thesis is attractive but should not treat all company growth as AI exposure.
keyRisk: AI-cooling economics are not separately disclosed and component-level value capture can be pressured by substitution, OEM insourcing, acquisitions and industrial-cycle sensitivity.
nextCatalyst: Conversion of elevated Climate & Sustainability Technologies bookings and expanded AI data-center heat-transfer capacity into reported revenue/earnings.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore is the weighted component total; risk and confidence are separately source-addressed for downstream methodology gates and are not silently folded into component values.
